categories.label: Frontend
categories.description: What users see and interact with — the screens, buttons, and forms that make up the user interface
categories.analogy: The storefront and customer-facing counters of a business. Everything the customer touches and sees.
signals: app/ or pages/ directory with page components
React, Vue, Svelte, or Angular components

categories.label: API Layer
categories.description: The gateway that receives all incoming requests and routes them to the right place — the front desk of your application
categories.analogy: The front desk at a hotel. Every guest request goes through the front desk, which figures out whether to call housekeeping, the restaurant, or the valet.

categories.label: Database
categories.description: Where your data lives permanently — the system of record that remembers everything even after restarts
categories.analogy: The filing cabinet that stores all your important records. Slower to access than your desk, but nothing gets lost.

categories.label: Cache
categories.description: A fast, temporary storage layer that keeps frequently accessed data close at hand to avoid slow database lookups
categories.analogy: A cookbook on the kitchen counter instead of in the bookshelf. Limited space, but anything there is instant to grab.

categories.label: Authentication and Authorization
categories.description: How the system verifies who you are and what you're allowed to do
categories.analogy: The security guard at the building entrance who checks your ID badge and makes sure you only go to floors you have access to.
signals: Clerk, Auth0, or other auth service SDK
Role/permission checks in middleware or routes

categories.label: External Services
categories.description: Third-party services your system depends on — payment processors, email providers, AI APIs, analytics, etc.
categories.analogy: Suppliers and contractors your business relies on. You don't make everything in-house — you outsource to specialists.
signals: HTTP client calls to external URLs
Third-party SDK imports (Stripe, SendGrid, Twilio, OpenAI, etc.)

categories.label: Background Jobs
categories.description: Tasks that run behind the scenes without making the user wait — sending emails, processing images, syncing data
categories.analogy: The back office that handles paperwork after the customer leaves. The customer doesn't wait while their receipt is filed and their loyalty points are updated.
signals: Background function handlers (Vercel cron, Inngest, Trigger.dev)

categories.label: File Storage
categories.description: Where files, images, documents, and uploads are kept — separate from the database
categories.analogy: The warehouse where you store physical inventory. Different from the office filing cabinet (database) — this is for bulky items.
signals: S3 or cloud storage client configuration
Cloudinary, Uploadthing, or image service SDK
Local file system write operations for user content
